lessons.title: Color theory and brand personality
lessons.concept: Understand hue, saturation, lightness, harmony, and contextual meaning instead of choosing a palette only by taste. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

explanation.title: Mental model
explanation.text: Understand hue, saturation, lightness, harmony, and contextual meaning instead of choosing a palette only by taste. explanation.title: Simple analogy
explanation.text: Color theory and brand personality is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Understand hue, saturation, lightness, harmony, and contextual meaning instead of choosing a palette only by taste. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: To master Color theory and brand personality, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.
